newsitem.title: TURKEY: Fading tension, c.bank grip may ease Turkey rates.
newsitem.headline: Fading tension, c.bank grip may ease Turkey rates.

text.p: The Turkish central bank's monetary policies and easing political tension are expected to lower bond yields in coming days, bankers said on Friday.
They say the central bank's hefty funding through overnight lending and repurchase agreements has eased the liquidity shortage in the market.
The bank's tight control over the money markets and frequent interventions have also eased an uptrend in rates last week when concerns about the future of the government mounted.

"The Turkish central bank is controlling the liquidity in the market via money market operations. I expect money and bond rates to go down in the coming days," said Erdogan Cicek, treasurer of private EGS Bank.
Average overnight money and repo rates rose by 4-5 points to 72-75 percent and bond yields surged around 10 points up to 100 percent in the past two weeks.
Bankers said bond yields of papers with 1998 maturity dates fell around one points on Friday. They expect the downtrend to continue.
"Bond yields will continue its downward trend next week due to easing liquidity squeeze and fading political worries. We may see 90 percent levels in the second week of May," Cicek said.
However, he still fears that any unexpected negative development on the political side might reverse the trend.
Speculation that the government of Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan was on the verge of collapse haunted Turkish markets last week.

Sentiment revived on Thursday after Erbakan's coalition partner Tansu Ciller pledged that she would stand by Erbakan despite a row with the military and the resignation of two ministers from her party.
"The DYP is not going to hide behind anyone and take part in action to topple the government," Ciller told a meeting of deputies from her True Path Party on Thursday.
The central bank also bought lira for dollars last week to curb dollar demand, boosted by political uncertainties and rising liquidity.
Bankers said the treasury was expected to hold an inflation-indexed bond auction next week to meet its bond redemeption of 130 trillion lira on May 7.
It sold only 10 trillion lira of two-year inflation-indexed bonds on Thursday. --Istanbul newsroom +90-212-275 08 75
